info.description: The fleet's governance record: governor receipts, Claude Code telemetry, sessions, installs, summaries and annotations, read per tenant under Enforcer credentials.
info.title: enforcer-governance API

get.description: Every key and root this service's proofs depend on, in one cacheable document, so a verifier can pin them instead of trusting the copy inside a proof bundle: the Ed25519 chain-head keys (primary and retired, purpose chain-head/v3), the RFC 3161 TSA roots pinned in the binary (subject and SHA-256 of the DER), the anchor leaf and statement format, and links to other services' key documents (enforcer-graph's GVNR step-seal keys). Canonically served at the host root, https://<api host>/.well-known/enforcer-keys.json; this path under the API prefix is the same document. No envelope: the top-level `keys` array is what governance-verify --keys accepts. Unauthenticated. Cache-Control public, max-age=300, with a strong ETag; If-None-Match answers 304.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: an ETag from an earlier response

get.description: Every account with activity in the window: decisions from the governor, spend (per session, the higher of Claude Code telemetry and the governor's receipt spend, counted once), tokens from telemetry, and its sessions. Rollup figures are hour-aligned (the hour containing `from` counts whole); sessions and first/last seen use the exact window, so this session count and /sessions' total agree. Each row carries display_name from enforcer-v3 (the short id when v3 cannot say in time; untrusted display text, one line, bounded) and, for a team lead (a caller who may write tenant-wide), email. `scope=tenant` needs tenant-wide read.

parameters.description: window end, RFC 3339, exclusive (default: now). Max span 400 days.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: csv of v3 group ids (max 10): only rows whose account is a member of one; ANDed with scope, so it only narrows. A group the caller cannot see is 404 group_not_found

parameters.name: exclude_group_id
parameters.description: csv of v3 group ids (max 10): drop rows whose account is a member of one

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: sort field, or a csv where a leading - means descending (e.g. -spend_usd,last_seen_at). Also accepts a v3-style named mode: `recent` | `oldest` | `costly` | `busiest`, which carries its own direction and cannot be combined with `order` or used inside a csv

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: sort direction for the single-field form

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: keyset cursor from a previous page's next_cursor; use the SAME sort

get.description: One account's activity, plus a zero-filled trend of decisions, asks, denies and spend. Buckets follow the request tz for day/week/month; hour buckets are UTC hours. An account with no activity in the window — or outside the caller's scope — is 404, not 403.

parameters.description: window end, RFC 3339, exclusive (default: now). Max span 400 days.

parameters.name: tz

parameters.name: bucket

get.description: A root the anchor pass built over signed chain heads (every tenant's, one tree per pass), the exact statement an RFC 3161 time service stamped, and that service's token. The statement is `enforcer-governance/anchor-root/v1`, the previous statement's SHA-256 (empty for the first), the tree size, the root hash and created_at, one per line; the token's imprint is SHA-256 of it. Follow `prev_statement_sha256` to walk the chain of roots. Unauthenticated: it carries no tenant data, and a verifier should not need a credential for the service it is checking. 404 `anchor_root_not_found` for an id that does not exist.
get.summary: One time-stamped Merkle root over signed chain heads

get.description: Notes visible to the caller. With target_id and no explicit from/to, every note on that target is returned regardless of age. Otherwise the window selects time_range notes that overlap it and other notes created inside it. scope=tenant needs tenant-wide read; scope=me (default) returns notes about the caller's data or written by the caller.

post.description:
Attach a note to a receipt, a session or an install, or to a period of time. target_id is the receipt id, the session's `id` (a uuid from listSessions — not its claude:xxxxxxxx ref, which two accounts can share) or the install id. The target must exist and be visible to the caller; otherwise 404 target_not_found (never 403, which would confirm it exists).

target_type `insight` acknowledges an Attention finding: target_id is its `fingerprint` from GET /insights, and the query names the digest it came from exactly as on GET /insights (scope, from, to, tz, account_id, group_id, exclude_group_id). The finding must be in that digest, else 404 target_not_found. scope=tenant needs tenant-wide write (else 403 insufficient_scope); scope=me (default) acknowledges a finding about the caller's own data. The body is optional and the label `ack` is always set. An acknowledgement is tenant-wide: GET /insights leaves the finding out for everyone until it is deleted (DELETE /annotations/{id} un-acknowledges). Acknowledging a finding that already has a live acknowledgement is not an error: 200 with the existing one.

parameters.description: insight only: whose digest the finding is in

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: insight only: the digest's window start, as on GET /insights

parameters.description: insight only: the digest's window end, as on GET /insights

get.description: The labels a diagnostics client offers on a note, in display order. Creating a note still accepts any label matching `^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$`; this list is the standard vocabulary, not a closed set. Readable by any authenticated caller.
One live note visible to the caller. Absent, archived and invisible are the same 404.

delete.description: Archives the note (it is never physically removed). Allowed for its author, or for a caller with tenant-wide write. Deleting an insight acknowledgement un-acknowledges the finding: GET /insights raises it again. A visible note the caller may not remove is 403 insufficient_scope.

patch.description: Change a note's body, labels, or (time_range notes only) its period. Only the author may edit; a visible note written by someone else is 403 insufficient_scope.

get.description: Recorded decisions on governor asks, highest seq (newest) first. A tenant-wide reader sees every decision in the tenant; anyone else sees decisions about their own agents' asks and the ones they made. `install` + `receipt_hash` together name one ask: the answer is zero or one item, which is how an edge polls for the decision on the ask it raised (verify `signature` over `message` with GET /chain-heads/public-keys). The plugin's ingest-only key (`governance:ingest`) may make exactly that one request, `install` + `receipt_hash` and no other parameter, and only for an install whose receipts it delivers; for any other install the answer is an empty page (READ_API.md §2k). Every other request with that key is 403 insufficient_scope.

post.description:
Records a human's decision on one stored receipt whose verdict is `ask`, named by its install and receipt hash (what the governor knows when it asks). The decision is the SERVER's record, not the edge's: who decided is the caller's own account (nothing in the body can name it), when is the database clock, and the row is appended to the tenant's approval hash chain and signed with the server's Ed25519 key under the message type `enforcer-governance/approval/v1` (READ_API.md §2k), verifiable with GET /chain-heads/public-keys.

Only a person may decide: an agent credential, an ingest-only key, a service principal or service account, a portal link, or a program acting as the person (an OAuth act claim) is 403 insufficient_scope. The caller must see the receipt (tenant-wide read, or it is their own agent's; else 404 receipt_not_found) and may write it (tenant-wide write, or their own agent's; else 403 insufficient_scope). The credential that delivered the session's receipts from the machine cannot decide its asks: 403 approver_is_requester. A receipt that is not an ask is 409 not_an_ask; an ask already decided is 409 already_decided — the first decision is final. With no signing key configured, 503 signing_unavailable: an unsigned approval is not recorded.

STEP-UP: the caller must have made a passkey assertion in the last 5 minutes — a v3 session token whose `amr` contains `passkey` and whose `auth_time` is that recent (a passkey sign-in, or re-running the passkey ceremony). Anything else, including an api key, is 403 step_up_required: prompt for the passkey and retry. Checked after the body is validated and before anything is read.

The tenant's policy (GET /settings/approvals) applies: an ask the server received more than `ask_expiry_seconds` ago (default 24 h) is 409 ask_expired; with `require_different_approver` on, the ask's own account, or the steward of the agent whose key reported it, is 403 approver_is_subject (enforcer-v3 unreachable for the steward check: 503 upstream_unavailable).
post.summary: Approve or deny a governor ask

get.description: Walks every recorded decision in seq order and checks: seq is one past the previous, prev_hash is the previous decision's hash, hash is sha256 of the message rebuilt from the stored fields, the Ed25519 signature verifies under a published server key, and the receipt it names is still the `ask` it was about (same id, install, seq, hash, session and account). `verified: true` means the server's record of who approved or denied what, and when, was not altered after it was signed. A failing row is reported once, by its first failure, and the walk continues from it as stored. At most 100,000 decisions are walked; a longer chain reports `truncated: true` and `verified: false`. Tenant-wide (the chain covers every account's decisions), so it needs tenant-wide read: anyone else is 403 insufficient_scope.
One recorded decision visible to the caller (the same rule as GET /approvals). Absent, another tenant's and invisible are the same 404.

The Ed25519 public keys this server countersigns receipt chain heads with, and the retired keys that signed older heads. Unauthenticated: a public key is meant to be distributed, and a verifier should not need a credential for the service it is checking. A countersignature proves the server's record of a chain was not altered after it was countersigned; it does not prove where the receipts came from. `signing: false` with no keys means countersigning is not configured.

The same rows listReceipts returns for the same filters, as a CSV file. Columns: id, occurred_at, received_at, account_id, session, install, seq, verdict, source, policy, rule, reason, tool, model, client, client_guessed, context_tokens, cost_usd, chained, chain_break, hash, prev_hash. Empty fields are nulls. Newest first. X-Export-Total reports how many rows matched and X-Export-Truncated is set when the cap cut the file short (that header is measured just before streaming, so a row arriving mid-export can make it off by one row).

get.description: Distinct values with counts for each requested field, top 50 by count, within the window and scope. Receipt fields count receipts from the hourly rollup, so the window is widened to whole hours; `summary` receipts (session ends) are excluded from every count except the verdicts facet. The models facet also lists models seen only in telemetry, with count 0 (count is always the receipt count). event_names counts raw telemetry events. statuses, has_asks and has_denies count sessions overlapping the window the way listSessions does (not hour-widened), using the derived session status. Those three always include their zeros, in a fixed order: active, stalled, failed, ended, and true then false.

get.description: The tenant's live capability rules, first match by position. Definitions are the tenant's, readable by any authenticated caller — the same as managed settings, because every install applies them. `receipts` and `last_seen_at` follow scope: they count decisions whose rule string equals the name (summaries excluded, hour-aligned), not a foreign key, so a renamed rule does not take its old counts with it. scope=tenant needs tenant-wide read. Disabled rules are listed; archived rules are not. `can.write_rules` is tenant-wide write.

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description: csv of v3 group ids (max 10): only decisions whose account is a member of one

parameters.name: exclude_group_id
parameters.description: csv of v3 group ids (max 10): drop decisions whose account is a member of one

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: csv of exact rule names (max 50): only those live rules, so a decision's rule string resolves to its rule (and id) in one read. total counts the matches; an unknown name is simply absent

post.description: Adds one capability rule. Needs tenant-wide write (`can.write_rules`): the rule binds every install, so write-own is not enough and a portal credential is refused. Position omitted appends one past the last live rule; an explicit position or a live name already in use is 409. A rewrite requires field, replace_from and replace_to; any other action must not send them. The edge evaluates match; this service stores it. At most 200 live rules.

get.description: One live capability rule. Absent, archived, malformed and another tenant's id are the same 404. Counts follow scope, as on the list.

delete.description: Archives the rule (it is not physically removed) and returns it with archived_at set. A later GET is 404. The name and position become available again. Needs tenant-wide write. Receipts that already named the rule are left as they were.

patch.description: Replaces the given fields and revalidates the whole row. Needs tenant-wide write. A live name or position already in use is 409. Changing the action away from rewrite clears field, replace_from and replace_to; sending those on a non-rewrite is 400 invalid_field. A pure enable or disable is audited as that verb; any other edit is updated. Does not rewrite receipts.

get.description: Who changed this rule, when, and the diff, newest first. An archived rule's history stays readable; an unknown id, another tenant's id and a malformed id are 404. Readable by any authenticated caller.

Every profile ingest judges this tenant's rows by, in the order it tries them: the tenant's own (oldest first), then the built-ins (`builtin: true`, read-only). `ceiling` is the highest provenance level the harness can reach with what its profile declares, computed rather than stored. Readable by any authenticated caller. An edit reaches ingest within a minute: each ingest process caches a tenant's profiles for up to one minute.
One profile, built-in or the tenant's. An unknown name, and a stored profile ingest would ignore, are the same 404.

put.description: Stores the tenant's profile under `harness`, replacing any profile already there: a field absent from the body is empty afterwards. 201 when it is new, 200 when it replaced one. The body's `harness`, when present, must equal the path's (400 harness_mismatch); a built-in's name is 409 harness_profile_builtin, because a tenant may add harnesses but not redefine ours; a profile ingest could not use (an empty name prefix, service name or scope, which would match rows that carry none) is 400 invalid_profile; an unknown field is 400 invalid_body. Needs tenant-wide write, so a `developer` (read-all, write-own) is refused. Ingest applies the change within a minute: each ingest process caches a tenant's profiles for up to one minute.
put.summary: Create or replace a harness profile

parameters.name: harness
parameters.description: harness name: 1-64 lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-'

delete.description: Removes the tenant's profile and returns what it was. A built-in cannot be deleted (409 harness_profile_builtin). Needs tenant-wide write, so a `developer` is refused. Rows already labelled keep their label; ingest stops using the profile within a minute, as each ingest process caches a tenant's profiles for up to one minute.

post.description: Sent by the governor at SessionStart so a session carries its project (`client`) even when it never produces a receipt. With `harness` and the full `session_id` it also registers the session (provenance level 2): the first announcement of a session is kept, a repeat returns it unchanged, and an announcement of the same session under another harness is stored and makes the session a contradiction. `client` may be omitted when the body registers. Tenant and account come from the credential: a caller can only attribute its own account's sessions. Never creates a session — the attribution is held until telemetry or a receipt creates the session row, and applied at once when the row already exists. A named project replaces a guessed one (leading `?`); nothing replaces a named project, so a repeated call is idempotent. Authenticates like OTLP ingest (any valid credential for the account). Unknown body fields are ignored.
post.summary: Attribute a session to a project, and register it

get.description: What a console should raise without being asked: spend spikes, deny bursts, high ask rates, chain breaks, unchained records, installs that went quiet, sessions under context pressure, and expensive sessions. Every finding has a stable `fingerprint`; a finding someone acknowledged (POST /annotations, target_type `insight`) is left out unless include=acknowledged, and comes back when it recurs. Every finding is a plain question over the hourly rollups, computed in one transaction so the digest cannot contradict itself, and carries the filters a console needs to open the rows behind it. Ranked by severity, then by size. Not paginated — it is a digest, bounded by `limit`.

get.description: Every head of the install's receipt chain the server countersigned, newest first: one per ingest batch that stored a receipt, while a signing key is configured. Each carries the exact signed message, so it can be checked offline against GET /chain-heads/public-keys. A head an anchor pass has covered also carries `anchor`: its RFC 6962 audit path into a Merkle root, that root's statement, and the RFC 3161 time stamp token over SHA-256(statement) (GET /anchor/roots/{id}); a head newer than the last pass, or every head while anchoring is off, has none. A countersignature proves the server's record was not altered after it was countersigned — not where the receipts came from. Install-wide (a head covers every account's receipts on the machine), so it needs tenant-wide read: anyone else is 403 insufficient_scope.
get.summary: List an install's countersigned chain heads

get.description: Walks the install's stored receipts in seq order and, at every countersigned head, checks two things: the Ed25519 signature is valid under a published server key, AND the stored receipts up to that seq still produce the signed rows digest and end at the signed head hash. `verified: true` means the server's record of this chain was not altered after it was countersigned. It does NOT prove where the receipts came from — the edge's machine is outside what any signature here can vouch for. When anchoring is on, every stored anchor is checked too, offline: the head as stored must rebuild the anchored leaf, the audit path must lead to the root, and the root's statement and time stamp token must verify; `anchored_heads` and `anchors_valid` count them (both absent when anchoring is off), and one that does not check out is an `anchor_mismatch` failure. A head not yet anchored is not a failure. Receipts after the latest countersigned head are counted in `unsigned_receipts`, are not protected, and make the answer `verified: false` with an `unsigned_tail` failure at the first of them; a hole in seq is a `receipts_gap` failure. A chain longer than 250,000 receipts is verified that far and reports `truncated: true` and `verified: false` (partial: it never reports `unsigned_tail`, because the walk did not reach the tail). Install-wide, so it needs tenant-wide read: anyone else is 403 insufficient_scope. A result is cached in-process for 60 seconds per tenant and install: a cached answer carries `cached: true` and the original walk's `verified_at`. At most one verification per install, and two per server, run at once; any request beyond that is 429 `verify_busy` with a Retry-After header, and is not queued.
get.summary: Verify an install's countersigned chain heads

get.description: A governance-proof-v1 or -v2 document (PROOF_BUNDLE.md) for seqs from_seq..to_seq: -v1 when every head and row of the range is message v2, -v2 once any is v3 (migration 049). Every stored receipt row as the exact text columns the countersignature of the head covering it digests (32 for v2, 40 for v3), every countersigned head in the range with its exact message and signature, each head's RFC 6962 inclusion path when anchored, the chain of RFC 3161-stamped root statements linking those anchors (with their tokens), the server's public keys, and a `limits` list of what the bundle cannot prove. `cmd/governance-verify` and `tools/verify-bundle/verify.mjs` check it with no database and no credential. Defaults: from_seq 1, to_seq the latest stored seq. At most 50,000 seqs per bundle (400 `range_too_wide`; export consecutive ranges and verify them together as one series, which checks the whole chain from genesis); to_seq beyond the chain is 400 `invalid_to_seq`, from_seq after to_seq 400 `invalid_range`, a chain with no receipt 400 `invalid_range`. For from_seq > 1 the start state (the digest and chain head just before it) is the server's word, bound only through the first signed head in the range; a from_seq more than 250,000 receipts after the last signed head before it is 400 `from_seq_unreachable`. Streamed: an error after the first byte truncates the document, which no verifier accepts. Install-wide, so it needs tenant-wide read: anyone else is 403 insufficient_scope. At most two bundles per server are written at once; beyond that 429 `bundle_busy` with Retry-After.
get.summary: Export an offline-verifiable proof bundle of an install's receipt chain

get.description: Walks the install's receipts in seq order and RECOMPUTES what the stored flags claim: that each chained receipt's prev_hash is the previous chained receipt's hash, that seq is contiguous, and that the chain_break flags match the walk. What it CANNOT check: a receipt's hash against its body, because the body is never stored — only the hash the edge sent. Under any scope but an unnarrowed tenant-wide one the walk sees only the caller's receipts on a shared machine, so it reports `partial: true` and its gaps and flag disagreements are expected. An install the caller has not reported from (without tenant-wide read) is 404, not 403.

One row per model: governor decisions (decisions, allows, asks, denies, sessions) joined with Claude Code telemetry (spend, tokens); spend also counts the governor's receipt spend where a session's receipts showed more than its telemetry. cost_per_1k_output_tokens is telemetry spend over telemetry tokens only. Models are normalized (a trailing "[1m]"-style suffix is stripped), and a model seen only in telemetry still appears, with zero decisions. Hour-aligned: the rollups are hourly, so the hour containing `from` counts whole. `tool` narrows the decision side only (telemetry carries no tool), and therefore also drops telemetry-only models. Session-end `summary` receipts are never counted. Max span 400 days.

client.description:
The project. A leading '?' marks one the governor guessed from the folder
name rather than found in its configured mapping. Optional when the body
registers the session instead.

harness.description:
The harness the session runs in: a built-in provenance profile name
(claude-code, codex, grok-cli, gemini-cli, cursor, hermes, openclaw) or

session_id.description:
The harness's own session id, in full. When the agent id carries a short
form of it after a ':' (claude:0f3c9a1b), that must be its prefix.

The id the session is held under. Normally the agent sent; an older
governor's 'claude:' id for a Grok or Codex session comes back as the
harness's own ('grok:0f3c9a1b'), the id its receipts and telemetry are

registration.description:
The registration as held after the request (the first announcement of a
session wins). Absent when the body registered nothing.

changed_by_name.description:

the short id when v3 cannot say, or when the caller may not see it).

by.description: By is the account that acknowledged it.

by_name.description:

a teammate's name.

id.description: ID is the annotation's id; DELETE /annotations/{id} un-acknowledges.

note.description: Note is the optional note left with the acknowledgement; null when none.

ack.description:
Ack is the finding's acknowledgement. Only present with
include=acknowledged, and only on a finding someone acknowledged.

baseline.description:
Baseline is what it was measured against — the median day, the average
hour, the tenant's ask rate; null when there is nothing to compare to.

delta_pct.description:
DeltaPct is (value - baseline) / baseline as a percentage; null when the
baseline is null or zero.

evidence.description:
Evidence carries the parameters a console needs to deep-link to the rows
behind the finding — a filter set for the matching list endpoint.

fingerprint.description:
Fingerprint identifies this finding across reads: the same kind, subject
and occurrence (the spike's day, the burst's hour, the last break, the
session) always gets the same one, and a recurrence gets a new one.
Acknowledge a finding with POST /annotations {target_type: "insight",
target_id: fingerprint}.

occurred_at.description:
OccurredAt is when the thing happened (the spike's day, the burst's hour,
the last break), not when it was computed.

subject_id.description:
SubjectID is the subject's identifier in its own screen's terms: an
account id, a project (client) name, a session id (uuid), an install id.

subject_type.description:

screen to open; `none` is a finding about the window itself.

value.description:

audit_path.description: AuditPath is the RFC 6962 inclusion path, hex, nearest sibling first.

root_id.description: RootID names an entry of the bundle's roots.

format.description:

"governance-proof-v2" (message v2 and v3).

generated_at.description:
GeneratedAt is when the server wrote the bundle (UTC, RFC 3339). Not
signed: it says when, not that.

heads.description: Heads are every signed head with from_seq <= seq <= to_seq, oldest first.

keys.description:
Keys are the server's chain-head public keys as it published them when it
wrote the bundle. A copy, not a trust anchor: pin or cross-check them.

limits.description: Limits is what this bundle cannot prove (PROOF_BUNDLE.md §6), in words.

message_version.description:
MessageVersion is the newest chain-head message format a head of the
bundle may be signed under: "v2" in governance-proof-v1 (every head is
v2), "v3" in governance-proof-v2 (each head is v2 or v3).

roots.description:
Roots are the anchor roots from the oldest one any head is anchored in to
the newest, every root in between included, in id order, so the chain of
statements (line 2 of each) links them. A root no head here is anchored in
carries no token: only its statement is needed to link the chain.

row_columns.description:
RowColumns names the columns of MessageVersion, in order
(chainsign.RowColumnNamesFor): 32 in -v1, 40 in -v2, where a v2 row
carries the first 32. A verifier refuses a bundle whose list differs:
the digest is defined over exactly these.

rows.description: Rows are the stored receipts with from_seq <= seq <= to_seq, in seq order.

tenant_id.description: TenantID is line 2 of every head's message.

anchor.description: Anchor is null until an anchor pass covered the head.

key_id.description: KeyID is the signer key id: line 8 of Message.

signature.description: Signature is base64 of the 64-byte Ed25519 signature over Message.

public_key.description: PublicKey is base64 of the 32-byte Ed25519 public key.

valid_from.description:

when a key started or stopped signing (a key is configured, not dated).

statement.description: Statement is the exact text the time stamp is over (5 lines).

tsa_token_b64.description:
TSATokenB64 is the RFC 3161 TimeStampToken (CMS, DER), base64; null for
a root that is here only to link the chain.

columns.description:
Columns are the row's values of its version's columns (32 for v2, 40 for
v3), as Postgres rendered them as text (null for NULL): exactly the input
of EncodeRow.

prev_hash.description:
PrevHash and Hash repeat columns 14 and 15, for reading; a verifier
requires them to agree.

version.description:
Version is the message version the row is digested under: that of the
first signed head at or after its seq in the install's chain (which may
be past to_seq), or the version the server signs new heads under when no
head covers it yet. Only in governance-proof-v2, where it is required;
absent in -v1, where every row is v2.

truncated.description:
Truncated is true when the chain is longer than the walk's bound; the
answer is then verified: false.

verified.description:

the one before it, its hash and signature check out under a published
key, and the receipt it names is still the `ask` it was about — and the
walk reached the end of the chain.

audit_path.description: AuditPath is the RFC 6962 inclusion path, hex, nearest sibling first.

tsa_url.description: TSAURL is the time service that answered.

primary.description: Primary is the key new heads are signed with.

public_key.description: PublicKey is base64 of the 32-byte Ed25519 public key.

retired.description: Retired keys verify heads they signed before and sign nothing new.

message_version.description:
MessageVersion is the format new heads are signed under ("v3" since
migration 049). Heads signed before keep, and verify under, their own.

signing.description: Signing is whether this server is countersigning new heads right now.

url.description: URL is host-relative when the service is on this host.

anchor.description:
Anchor is where this head sits in an RFC 3161-timestamped Merkle root;
absent until an anchor pass has covered it (or when anchoring is off).

head_hash.description:
HeadHash is the last chained receipt's hash at seq; null while the chain
had only unchained records.

message.description:
Message is the exact bytes that were signed, rebuilt from the fields above,
so a verifier outside this service needs only the public key.

rows_digest.description:
RowsDigest is the running sha256 over the stored receipt rows 1..seq, each
row the columns of chainsign.RowColumns that the version of the head
covering it digests: 32 for v2, 40 for v3 (READ_API.md §2g lists them).

signature.description: Signature is base64 of the 64-byte Ed25519 signature over Message.

signed_at.description: SignedAt is exactly as it appears in the message: UTC, six fractional digits.

version.description:
Version is the message format the head was signed under: line 1 of
Message.

sha256.description: SHA256 is the lower-case hex SHA-256 of the certificate's DER.

anchored_heads.description:
AnchoredHeads counts the signed heads included in an RFC 3161-timestamped
Merkle root (READ_API.md §2g, migration 044); AnchorsValid those whose
inclusion path, root statement and time stamp token all check out. Both
null when anchoring is not enabled on this server. A head newer than the
last anchor pass is legitimately unanchored and is not a failure; an
anchor that does not check out is (anchor_mismatch).

cached.description:
Cached is true when this answer was computed by an earlier request, at
most 60 seconds ago, and served without walking the chain again.
verified_at is then that earlier walk's time, not this request's.

contiguous.description: Contiguous is whether seq ran 1, 2, 3 … with no hole.

failures.description:
Failures are what did not verify, oldest seq first, at most 50: a signed
head (signature or receipts), a gap in seq (receipts_gap), or receipts
after the latest signed head (unsigned_tail).

latest_signed_seq.description: LatestSignedSeq is the highest seq countersigned; null when none is.

signatures_checked.description: SignaturesChecked / SignaturesValid count the signed heads the walk reached.

truncated.description:
Truncated is true when the chain is longer than one walk's cap: heads past
it were not checked (SignaturesChecked says how many were), and the tail
was not looked at, so unsigned_tail is never reported with it. A truncated
walk is partial, never verified.

unsigned_receipts.description:
UnsignedReceipts are receipts after the latest countersigned head (stored
while signing was off, or not yet signed). Nothing protects them.

verified.description:
Verified is true when at least one head was checked, every checked head's
signature is valid, the stored receipts still digest and chain to what
each one signed, seq is contiguous, the walk was not truncated, and no
receipt is stored after the latest countersigned head (unsigned_tail). It
says the server's record was not altered after it was countersigned. It
says NOTHING about where the receipts came from.

enabled.description: Enabled is whether this server runs anchor passes.

imprint.description: Imprint is what the time stamp token is over.

leaf_format.description:
LeafFormat is a leaf's first line; the leaf is it, the head's 8-line
message and the base64 signature, joined by "\n".

root_url.description: RootURL fetches one stored root, host-relative.

statement_format.description: StatementFormat is a root statement's first line.

statement_lines.description:
StatementLines names the statement's five lines in order, joined by
"\n" with no trailing newline.

tsa_roots.description: TSARoots are the roots a token must chain to, sorted by fingerprint.

message_prefix.description: MessagePrefix is the first line of every signed head message.

public_keys_url.description: PublicKeysURL is the same keys in the API's envelope, host-relative.

signing.description: Signing is whether this server is countersigning new heads right now.

public_key.description: PublicKey is base64 (standard, padded) of the 32-byte Ed25519 public key.

purpose.description:
Purpose is what the key signs now: chain-head/v3 is the message in
chain_heads[].message (first line enforcer-governance/chain-head/v3). Heads
signed before 049 carry v2 messages and verify under the same key.

keys.description: Keys are the chain-head keys, sorted by key_id, retired ones included.

has_asks.description:
HasAsks and HasDenies count sessions, value "true" then "false", zeros
included. The window is the exact overlap listSessions uses.

statuses.description:
Statuses counts sessions by the derived status listSessions returns,
in the order active, stalled, failed, ended. Zeros are included.
paused and grounded are not chips; they still appear on the session row.

can.description:
Can is what this caller may do. write_settings is tenant-wide write;
a developer and a portal credential both have it false.

managed.description:
Managed is false when no tenant settings exist, so a client can tell
"nothing is managed" from "everything happens to be at its default".

settings.description:

spent_usd or summary cost_usd they carried). Null when nothing reported a
cost (CostSource "none"). CostSource "summary" is the closing receipt's
figure, "receipts" the running spend of a session's decisions; both are
whole-session running totals, not windowed.

active. Null once a summary has ended it, or when it has no decision yet.

of quiet; current still carries the last decision, so judge freshness
from current.at.

first 8 characters) when v3 cannot say in time. Null only when AccountID is.

never instructions.

tenant-wide); null for anyone else, a developer's key included.

errors.description: Errors is api errors plus failed tool results. A deny is not an error.

latest telemetry or receipt was attributed to ("unknown" when no profile
matched). Null when nothing stamped says, as for sessions reported before
harnesses were recorded.

its row does not exist yet.

peak_context_tokens.description: PeakContextTokens / LastContextTokens are context-size snapshots, not usage.

provenance_level.description:
ProvenanceLevel is how much of this session's origin is proven: -1
contradiction, 0 authenticated, 1 shaped, 2 registered (announced by the
governor at session start), 3 corroborated (announced, and both its
telemetry and its receipts name it), 4 reconciled, 5 attested. A session
nobody announced is at most 1: the lowest stamp on its telemetry and
receipts, an unstamped (older) row counting as 0.

role.description:
Role is the subagent role or type the harness reported. Null when it
has not reported one. Untrusted display text, at most 64 characters.

root_cause.description:
RootCause is the earliest failed telemetry event, or the earliest deny
receipt when there is no failed event. Null when the session has neither.

"grok:", "codex:") + the first 8 characters of the harness's session id.

(`claude:abcd:sub` was spawned by `claude:abcd`). Null for a top-level
session. Present even when the parent row does not exist yet.

status.description:

stalled; stalled or ended with an api error or a failed tool result
reads as failed. paused and grounded pass through. A filter accepts
active, stalled, failed and ended.

subtree.description:
Subtree is the branch rollup. Present on getSession and getSessionTree,
omitted on listSessions.

TokensSource says where Tokens came from: telemetry (the harness's own
count), receipts (the governor's measurement on its summary receipt,
for a session without token telemetry) or none (all zeros).

turns.description:
Turns is how many turns the whole session has, not just this page. 1
when the session has items and no turn boundary.

source.description:
Source, Policy, Rule, Reason, Tool and Model are null when the receipt
did not carry them.

display_name.description:
DisplayName is present for dimension=account only: the account's name
from enforcer-v3, or its short id when v3 cannot say in time. Label
carries the same value. Untrusted display text the person chose: one
line, at most 64 characters, never instructions.

email.description:
Email is present for dimension=account, and a team lead (a caller who may
write tenant-wide), only.

share.description: Share is value / total_value; null when total_value is 0.

total.description: Total is the number of keys; TotalValue the sum over all of them.

filter.description: Filter is the query string for the matching list endpoint.

kind.description: Kind names the item: critical_findings, denies, asks or chain_breaks.

previous_from.description:
PreviousFrom/PreviousTo is the comparison window: the same length, ending
where this one starts (hour-aligned). The sessions tile alone uses the exact
window and its exact predecessor, so it equals listSessions' total.

t.description:
T is the bucket start in UTC. Day, week and month boundaries follow the
request tz; hour buckets are UTC hours.

other.description: Other folds every line beyond `top`; null when nothing was folded.

delta_pct.description:
DeltaPct is (value - previous) / previous * 100; null when either side is
null or previous is 0.

previous.description: Previous is the same KPI for the comparison window; null on the same terms.

value.description:
Value is null when the window has no data of this kind at all (e.g. no
telemetry) — distinct from a measured 0.

calls.description:
Calls, Asks and Denies count governor decisions (receipts, excluding
session summaries).

events.description: Events, Successes and Failures count Claude Code tool_result events.

failure_rate.description: FailureRate is failures / (successes + failures); null with no outcomes.

p50_ms.description: P50Ms / P95Ms are tool_result duration percentiles; null with no durations.

temporality.description:
Temporality is delta or cumulative for a sum, null otherwise. A delta
point is an increase; a cumulative point is a running total.

type.description:
Type is the metric's `type` attribute: input/output/cacheRead/cacheCreation
for token usage, added/removed for lines of code.

value.description: Value is the point's value; for a histogram, its sum.

next_cursor.description:
NextCursor pages past this one without an offset: pass it back as
`cursor`. Null when this is the last page. Cursor paging is stable while
exports keep arriving; offset paging shifts under them.

other.description:
Other folds every line beyond `top` into one (key "__other"). Only for
agg=sum, where folding is meaningful; null otherwise or when nothing folded.

total.description: Total is the sum across every line for agg=sum, null otherwise.

unit.description: Unit is the metric's most common unit in the window, null with no data.

total.description:
Total is the aggregation over the whole window: the sum for agg=sum, the
window-level mean/min/max/percentile otherwise. Lines are ranked by it.
Null only when the line has no value at all.

t.description:
T is the bucket start in UTC. Day, week and month boundaries follow the
request tz; hour buckets are UTC hours.

value.description:
Value is null for a bucket with no data under any aggregation other than
sum (a mean or percentile of nothing is not zero); sum buckets with no data
are 0.

attributes.description: Attributes is every attribute as sent, including the nested resource.

body.description:
Body is as exported. Claude Code redacts prompt text unless
OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS is set, and the governor never sets it.

next_cursor.description:
NextCursor pages past this one without an offset: pass it back as
`cursor`. Null when this is the last page. Cursor paging is stable while
exports keep arriving; offset paging shifts under them.

position.description: Position omitted means append (one past the last live rule).

archived_at.description:
ArchivedAt is null on a live rule. DELETE sets it and returns the row;
a later GET is 404. The revision history of an archived rule stays readable.

field.description: Field, ReplaceFrom and ReplaceTo are set only for a rewrite.

last_seen_at.description:
LastSeenAt is the latest rollup HOUR a decision named this rule, same
scope as Receipts. Null when none have. Hour-aligned, like /rules.

receipts.description:
Receipts counts decisions whose rule string equals name, over the caller's
scope. It is not a foreign key: renaming or archiving this row does not
change a receipt. Summaries are excluded.

can.description: Can is the caller's action set, present on an empty page too.
